For a sector i, complete positivity of T_i(X)=d_i Tr(X)I-X follows from Choi d_i I⊗I-|Omega_i><Omega_i| >= 0 (|Omega_i|^2=d_i). For any reference, eta_i^(RA_i) <= d_i rho_R⊗I_(A_i), hence the target block is <= S rho_R⊗(sigma_*)_i with S=sum d_i^2 and sigma_* sector weight d_i^2/S. The resulting common positive part of normalized target and replacer states weighs at least 1/S, giving diamond upper bound 2(1-1/S). For any replacer sigma with sector weights q_i, some i has q_i/d_i^2<=1/S; a maximally entangled RA_i input and binary effect |Phi_i><Phi_i|⊗I_(B_i) have ideal probability 1 versus replacer q_i/d_i^2, giving matching diamond lower bound. For flagged probability p the same witness yields 2p(1-1/S), and the upper construction is scaled by p. The argument handles arbitrary entangled references, any positive gauge m_i, S=1 and p=0,1, and uses UNHALVED diamond norm. It does not rely on a finite test or unproved general channel optimization.
